/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 26 August 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 3056 (130)
Baltic Capesize Index: 5033 (298)
Baltic Panamax Index: 2246 (80)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1644 (1)
Baltic Handysize Index: 880 (3)
CAPESIZE
Another positive day for the market, with the upward trajectory maintained and sentiment remaining firmly constructive. The BCI 5TC gained $2,706 to $45,651, supported by strength in both the Pacific and Atlantic basins. The C5 index rose 0.775 to $15.245, while C3 increased 0.464 to $37.555. The Pacific market remained firm, with three miners in the market and healthy operator volume underpinning sentiment. Fixture activity was relatively limited, however, with owners showing resistance to prevailing bid levels as offers were generally heard in the mid-to-high $15s, depending on actual ETA. One miner was reported fixed in the low $15s, while an operator was understood to have paid $15.30. The Atlantic basin also strengthened, supported by firmer C3 fixtures. In the North Atlantic, a stronger trans-Atlantic round voyage reported overnight helped lift the C8 index by $4,218 to $48,781, while improved fronthaul demand drove the C9 index up by $3,389 to $79,333. Activity in the Atlantic has also picked up noticeably, with reports of $37.50 fixed yesterday for end-September loading and interest now extending into October. On index dates today, bids were heard in the mid-$37s against offers in the high $37s.

PANAMAX
A far more positive day as we pass the midpoint of the week with the P5TC average up $717 to settle at $20,213, with P6 up almost $1,000 today. In the Atlantic many said the market was fairly quiet, but rates have seen a surge today as realisation that there have been trades concluded in excess of the index. Fronthaul demand comfortably exceeds transatlantic demand, but sentiment has definitely changed on the whole. It was a busy start to the day in the South with rates for second half September fronthaul now comfortably over $20,000, and sources also pointed to the fact that October positions are now showing interest in fixing forward in order to take advantage of the upturn. The positiveness in the East also remained, with NoPac grains and Australian minerals the main drivers, but there was also more Indonesian coal cargoes to India which has added support the cargoes to China. Period activity was also evident with the Gia Aspirant (82,000 2026 ) Yangzhou end August said to have fixed one year at $21,000, although further details did not come to light, and the Shi Dai 11 (75,467 2012) Sual end August said to have fixed to Oldendorff for 5 to 7 months, but no rate was revealed.
SUPRAMAX
As we pass midweek the market continues to lack much direction with the 11TC average again showing a minimal gain of $19 to close at $20,784. The North Americas saw more activity which has stemmed the recent decline in rates, whilst the Continent was said to be steady, albeit with very little transparency. The Mediterranean remained under pressure without sufficient fresh demand to absorb the lengthy tonnage list and the South Atlantic might now be showing some fragility as activity has slowed. In Asia the sentiment appeared more positive with levels being maintained or slightly up, but there wasn’t much change with the NoPac and backhaul markets looking well balanced. The Genco Enterprise (63,997 2016) CJK fixed a trip via Nopac to WC Soth America at $19,000 for the first 65 days, but the rate for the balance and the Charterer were unknown, and the SSI Dauntless (57,200 2013) Singapore 27-30 August was said to have fixed a sugar cargo to Indonesia at $16,000.
HANDYSIZE
The Handysize market remained subdued through midweek, with activity levels generally limited across most regions. The HS7TC gained 40 on the day to close at $15,834.

Despite the quieter backdrop, sentiment in the US Gulf continued to strengthen, supported by a tight tonnage list and improving bid levels. Market participants also noted increasing demand for larger Handysize vessels in the region, helping to underpin rates. In contrast, the Continent and North Atlantic markets saw little fresh activity, with fixture volumes remaining sparse and rates largely unchanged. Some support was evident for prompt tonnage, but overall momentum remained limited.

In the North Atlantic, ES Honesty (37,052 dwt, 2014) fixed basis Skaw on a trip to Matadi at $16,500 daily to Norden, while K Sukret (33,814 dwt, 2014) secured $15,850 daily from Liverpool for a Skaw trip via the Baltic with redelivery Luanda to Navision. Chrysoula S (37,786 dwt, 2015) was reported on subjects from Bilbao for a voyage via Murmansk to Klaipeda carrying fertilisers at $17,000 daily.

In Asia, activity remained steady rather than spectacular. An Hai Confidence (37,405 dwt, 2012) was reported on subjects from Pomalaa for a trip via Indonesia with redelivery Taiwan carrying clinker at $15,000 daily. Ocean Spring (33,633 dwt, 2010) was heard fixed from Jakarta for an Australian round voyage with grains at $15,000 daily to Norden.

Market Fundamentals
Fenix Resources Q2 Results

In its latest earnings report, Australian miner Fenix Resources reported record annual production (+1.7 Mt to 4.4 Mt) and shipments (+2.0 Mt to 4.4 Mt), in FY25/26 (July to June). The company attributed the record year to efficiency improvements, including improved inland logistics alongside a new expanded shipping capacity through its arrangement with partner Mira Bulk.

Trading Commentary
Cape
The Cape curve was active but mixed through the session today. September was again the main focus, trading between 43,500–44,900, with most activity concentrated around 44,500–44,750 before easing back to 44,000 late in the day. October traded between 45,000–45,800, with repeated clips around 45,500–45,750. Q4 26 traded between 43,500–44,250, with the market softening through the session and majority of the activity seen around 43,500. The Sep v Q4 spread widened and strengthened up to 850 today. Q1 27 traded between 29,700–30,150, while Cal 27 printed at 33,150 and Cal 28 traded between 29,200–29,300. Further out, Q3+Q4 27 printed at 34,100.
